value.body: A three-year, skills-based bachelor's degree in one trade, such as retail, tourism, healthcare technology, software or media. Most of the credits go to hands-on skill training and on-the-job learning, linked to the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF). Universities and colleges run it under UGC and AICTE schemes.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Exit points: diploma after 1 year, advanced diploma after 2 years (NSQF levels 5–7)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12; some trades need specific subjects, and some colleges also take ITI or diploma holders. Admission is mostly by Class 12 merit or a university's own process. Some central universities, such as MANUU and the Central University of Kashmir, use CUET-UG.

value.title: At a glance
items: A UGC notice (2016) asks that B.Voc be treated on par with other bachelor's degrees for UPSC, SSC and state PSC exams.
The trade you choose shapes your job options more than the degree name.
An M.Voc, or any master's open to graduates (such as an MBA), can follow.

value.title: B.Voc enrolment by year
value.note: AISHE counts are based on institutions' own responses.
